PullRequest.Title: sessions: inspect a session's customizations on phones
PullRequest.Body:

On phones, open **Customizations** from a session's drawer menu to read its instructions, skills, and agents without switching chats. The inspector shows what that session's host has reported. It doesn't wake an unattached cloud environment, substitute the active chat's items, or offer install and edit actions. An incomplete or unavailable list is not shown as an empty one.

### Try it with a real session

1. Sign in to the Agents workbench in a phone layout. Leave a recognizable unsent draft in session A.
2. From the drawer, open the menu for a different, connected session B and choose **Customizations**. Open an item you know belongs to B and check its source if available.
3. Use **Back** to return to the list, then the drawer. Close the drawer: A should still be active with its draft unchanged.

The draft-preservation flow was verified with sample data in iPhone-emulated WebKit. A signed-in, physical-phone check is still pending.

### Validation on `5495ab0cf0c`

- `npm run transpile-client` and `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` and `npm run check-mobile-boundary` — passed (120 reviewed contributions).
- The following command passed **99 tests in Chromium and 99 in WebKit**, including shared Accessible View, the inspector, and local and attached-cloud routing:

```sh
node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --browser webkit \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/mobile/test/browser/mobileCustomizationsInspector.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/mobile/mobilePickerSheet.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/accessibility/test/browser/accessibleView.test.ts \
  --grep 'MobileCustomizationsInspector|AgentCustomizationItemProvider|MobilePickerSheet|MobileContentSheet|inspecting customizations|AccessibleView' --reporter dot
```

- Eight regression cases passed in macOS Electron 43.8.10, including the **Back after refresh** case that previously timed out. With `ELECTRON` pointing to the matching Code - OSS binary:

```sh
"$ELECTRON" test/unit/electron/index.js \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/mobile/test/browser/mobileCustomizationsInspector.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentCustomizationItemProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/accessibility/test/browser/accessibleView.test.ts \
  --grep 'MobileCustomizationsInspector|projects only confirmed session children|updating the content keeps focus' --timeout 6000
```

- In iPhone-emulated WebKit with sample inventory, the live Accessible View updated from loading to the list, kept keyboard focus on refresh, and returned to the replacement row or Back on Escape. The shared focus regression failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Commit hygiene passed on all seven changed files.
- `npm run gulp -- compile-client` — blocked before compilation: the shared local dependency installation bundles Copilot runtime `1.0.113-1`, but the checkout declares `1.0.114`.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Traced the new inspector through observeSessionCustomizations and the subscription manager to AgentService.subscribe's missing-snapshot branch, then through the explicit full restore and awaited provider history read. Listed sessions need not be restored: _announceSurfacedSession publishes summaries separately. Existing subscriptions are refcounted, so this finding specifically concerns cold sessions, not every opening or every customization.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Default-chat transcript reads and hydrated turn objects; provider runtime initialization when required by the restore.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One coalesced restore per selected cold session, with transcript work growing with that chat's history, not with the number of customization rows. Warm existing subscriptions are shared and avoid this restore.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The customization list remains loading behind unrelated chat restoration, with additional host I/O and turn-object allocation for large histories.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Catalog/drawer inspection did not restore a selected inactive chat for customization details, and getCustomizations only returned already-known _lastSessionStates data. Full restoration was associated with paths that needed the chat rather than this new inventory-only reader.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Opening the read-only inspector for a listed but host-unrestored session now issues a restoring session subscription and waits for full default-chat hydration before receiving its inventory.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new acquireSessionCustomizationState method calls connection.getSubscription(StateComponents.Session, cached.backendUri, 'SessionCustomizations') at line 7877 for any eligible catalog-cached session. Previously getCustomizations immediately above only read _lastSessionStates; opening the drawer did not acquire a session subscription for inspection.
Findings.Title: Avoid restoring the entire chat for cold customization inspection
Findings.Impact: After reconnecting to a host or selecting an inactive session whose state has been evicted, opening Customizations can wait for SDK initialization and the selected chat's entire transcript to be read and hydrated. Long-running chats therefore incur history-sized I/O, allocation, and latency merely to display the inventory.
Findings.Evidence: MobileCustomizationsInspector.open calls observeSessionCustomizations at mobileCustomizationsInspector.ts:177; that method acquires this reference and waits for sub.verifiedValue. AgentSubscriptionManager.getSubscription (agentSubscription.ts:1130-1183) sends subscribe on a cache miss. AgentService.subscribe (agentService.ts:12072-12090) restores a missing session snapshot; _doRestoreSession invokes _restoreSessionState with { kind: 'full' } at 14705. That path awaits agent.materializeChat at 14980 and _getChatMessages at 15190, which awaits provider.chats.getMessages and hydrateTurns at 10861-10870. Copilot's _getChatMessages (copilotAgent.ts:9694-9744) can resolve/resume the runtime; its persisted-history path also reads the journal in pages (9778 onward). None of this chat history is consumed by the inspector.
Findings.Recommendation: Reuse an already-held session snapshot for inspection and show unavailable for cold sessions until a passive inventory capability is available, rather than creating a normal restoring subscription from this read-only path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Customizations for a catalog-listed native session that is cold on the connected host.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The sheet opens immediately, but inventory readiness waits for getSubscription -> subscribe -> missing-snapshot restoration -> full default-chat materialization and history hydration -> subscription snapshot -> projection and DOM rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the selected session's initial state snapshot over the agent connection (local IPC or remote network transport).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for an uncached backend session subscription, shared with concurrent holders; reconnect transport recovery may retry according to existing protocol behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Catalog/drawer browsing did not acquire an inspection subscription; getCustomizations only read already-known state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The inventory waits for the initial verified snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore registry/catalog/configuration, chat contributions, transcript state, and annotations for the selected session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced full restore on a host snapshot miss, involving per-session database lookups and default-chat history hydration; transcript work grows with history. Not one restore per customization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This full restore was not requested by a customization-only drawer inspection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Full restoration is awaited before the session snapshot is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the provider's default-chat history, potentially resolve/resume its runtime, and hydrate returned turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical history read for the selected cold session; Copilot persisted journals are paged in batches of up to 1000 events. Actual runtime startup depends on provider and credential/cache state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inventory-only drawer use did not request provider chat history or runtime resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by full restoration despite the inspector not consuming chat history.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicitly selected session, its default-chat transcript size/turn count, and its customization inventory. History work is not bounded by the number of customization rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One subscription per backend session URI is shared by reference count. Host restores join an in-flight restore for the same session. Provider history and workspace-transition reads can overlap; there is no per-customization subscription fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A catalog cache entry is not a hydrated session snapshot. A client subscription miss sends subscribe; a host snapshot miss performs full restore. An existing subscription avoids the wire request, and an existing host snapshot avoids full restoration. The inspector does not repeatedly retry errors per row.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the new acquire through missing client and host snapshots to the explicit full-restore branch and awaited provider history hydration. Catalog publication separately supports unhydrated sessions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold-session prevalence, provider startup time, transcript sizes, and hardware vary; no measured latency is asserted.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity eager-work regression: unrelated full-chat restoration blocks a cold inventory-only inspection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Inspect an already-hydrated session locally or through an attached cloud runtime, receive inventory updates, and close or return from details.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Read the shared verified session state, project published children, normalize/sort the three visible sections, and rebuild the list. Detail navigation does not activate the selected chat in the client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Share or acquire one state stream for the selected backend resource and unsubscribe when its final holder closes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero additional subscribe calls when another healthy holder already exists; otherwise one subscribe, plus one final unsubscribe only when the reference count reaches zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No phone inspection holder existed; other subscription holders already shared the same manager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Warm shared state can render synchronously. An unshared but host-warm state requires the snapshot round trip, without full restore.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The selected session's published containers/children and at most three section normalizations; DOM rows scale with published inspected items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session subscriptions are refcounted by backend URI. A nested autorun observes inventory changes without reacquiring for every row or ordinary snapshot update. Per-run stores dispose replaced row listeners; closing releases the reference.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm client subscriptions add a reference without a new subscribe. Inventory and roots are separately mapped with reference equality, so unchanged inventory/roots do not reconstruct the list for unrelated state changes. No ambient management-inventory fallback.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for refcounting, equality suppression, listener replacement, and close ownership based on implementation and added routing/lifetime cases.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Largest real inventories and refresh frequency were not measured. Full-list rendering is linear plus per-section sorting, but no additional high-confidence hot-event multiplier was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: ordinary warm use has one grouped stream and bounded-by-inventory rendering; cleanup and refresh ownership are present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open inspection for an unattached cloud task, offline host, legacy adoptable row, policy-disabled provider, or provider without exact-session inventory support.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the explicitly selected session's owning provider/harness and display an unavailable, unsupported, or connection-status message.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected drawer row; harness/provider catalog lookup, not all sessions or all environments.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No environment-acquisition operation is scheduled. Availability gates prevent inventory observation when offline/loading/unsupported, and the provider rejects policy-disabled or legacy-adoptable sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses already-registered providers and advertised catalog state. There is no fallback to active-session inventory and no per-item negative-cache retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the changed guards, owner routing, and local/attached-cloud cases in the added tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful boundary-duration uncertainty for the gated paths; attached-runtime cold restoration is covered separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression on unavailable/unattached paths; they do not wake an unattached environment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an instruction, skill, or agent's source and navigate Back.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Open the detail sheet, read only the chosen readable URI, decode and strip front matter, then synchronously parse/sanitize/render its Markdown. Back is available while the read is pending.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat/resolve and read the chosen source file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical file read plus metadata validation per explicit readable-detail opening; zero reads for non-readable items or unselected rows. Validation and unbuffered content reading can overlap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no phone detail-reader path; no inventory-wide source read has been introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only source content waits; sheet presentation and Back do not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve ordinary remote-file metadata and fetch Base64-encoded content through resourceRead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a normal remote source, one resourceResolve and one resourceRead; virtual content refs use synthetic stat and need only resourceRead. Connection recovery can use existing retries. Not multiplied by inventory size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This remote filesystem provider and its limiter already existed; the new detail view adds a demand-driven caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected source awaits its content response; the provider's read limiter can queue it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Decode remote bytes, convert text, parse front matter, and render sanitized Markdown into DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successful explicit source opening. The allowed-tag override excludes images, so rendered source does not introduce image-fetch fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No phone source-reader render existed; no background pre-render of all items has been added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Text conversion and rendering run on the UI thread after the file read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Chosen source-file bytes and Markdown complexity, with accepted/rendered content limited to 1 MiB. Source reads are not eager across the inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One read per explicit detail opening, not one read per list row. Remote AHP reads use the existing provider-wide limiter of 10. Close cancels the caller and disposed-sheet checks suppress rendering; an already-issued unbuffered remote RPC need not be interrupted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The inspector has no persistent source cache; revisiting issues another explicit read. Provider/source type determines local versus remote handling. The file-service size limit rejects oversized accepted content, but unbuffered remote reads can receive the full file before checking it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for demand-driven cardinality, byte-validation placement, limiter scope, and disposal checks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Source-size distribution and parse duration on physical phones are unknown. No large-file prevalence or measured rendering stall is assumed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence regression: source work is explicitly requested and scoped to one item. The existing remote unbuffered-read behavior is not reported as a new independent bug.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read a live inspector list/source through Accessible View, including refresh and dismissal.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On first Accessible View request, lazily create a mutation observer, read rendered sheet text, and update the accessible editor model when the body changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read innerText across browser layout and replace the accessible editor's model content when changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On explicit accessible-content display and subsequent mutation notifications for that page; the observer is lazy, not per inventory row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No inspector-specific accessible content existed. Shared accessible rendering already read provider content; its changed append guard removes a redundant DOM move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the accessible-content presentation/update path; normal inspection does not install this observer eagerly.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered sheet text and actual body updates, rather than all sessions. The editor still performs its existing content/model work per update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The shared mutation observer groups DOM mutations into observer callbacks. It is not created until accessible content is requested. Page stores own observer disposal; provider focus restoration uses current row lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: One lazy content-change event per page. The shared Accessible View change avoids re-appending its existing container when it already has the correct parent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lazy observer creation and ownership. The shared append guard primarily fixes focus; no distinct proven historical performance regression is claimed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM size and accessible-content update frequency were not profiled. No animation/frame-frequency source was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression or regression-fix learning signal: no high-frequency self-trigger or lost disposal was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Phone entry/menu registration and existing desktop customization-management reads.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Register the phone action and accessible providers during module loading; construct the inspector and acquire its state only after the user runs the action. Desktop management continues its existing directory conversion path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed action/provider registration; desktop conversion still scales with directory children and existing working-directory matching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No startup subscription or source-read loop is added. Existing management conversion remains synchronous and collection-based; moving source/scope inference into the helper preserves its once-per-directory placement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new global inventory/content cache or unbounded retained collection is added. Inspector page bookkeeping uses a WeakMap plus explicit deletion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for action-driven allocation and the behavior-preserving conversion refactor.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Module-loading byte/timing differences were not measured; no concrete new startup filesystem/network/runtime work was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup or desktop-management regression found.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 21-file inventory and every diff page, then traced the performance-review scenarios through subscription sharing/restoration, provider history, source filesystem transport, rendering, accessibility, and disposal. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity finding for full-chat restoration on cold inventory-only inspection. No other candidates met the performance causality/evidence threshold. Static read-only review; no measured timing claims or code changes.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
